items.title: BlackRock: AI Agents to Drive Next Wave of Stablecoin Adoption
points: BlackRock identifies autonomous AI agents (self-operating software programs that execute decisions without human input) as a major growth driver for stablecoin (cryptocurrency pegged to stable assets like the US dollar) adoption.
AI agents need fast, programmable settlement, and stablecoins avoid the price volatility that would disrupt automated financial workflows.
BlackRock projects agent-to-agent commerce could generate far more stablecoin transaction volume than current human-driven activity.
Multiple blockchain networks are racing to optimize infrastructure for high-frequency, agent-based settlement and clearing.
Institutional investment in stablecoin infrastructure is accelerating as traditional finance prepares for agent-driven transactions.

items.title: Canadian Banks Launch Tokenized Deposit Initiative
points: Canada's six major banks (BMO, CIBC, National Bank, RBC, Scotiabank, TD) are jointly exploring a Canadian-dollar tokenized deposit system (digital representation of bank deposits on a blockchain).
First phase focuses on moving tokenized deposits efficiently between institutions.
Move follows Canada's regulator (OSFI) clarifying tokenized deposits carry the same legal status as traditional deposits.
Builds on March's Project Samara pilot, which tested blockchain-based government bond issuance.

items.title: CFTC Warns on Prediction Market Manipulation Risks
points: CFTC's Division of Market Oversight says prediction contracts betting on specific word mentions or event attendance carry heightened manipulation risk.
Such contracts can only be listed in limited circumstances under the Commodity Exchange Act.
CFTC has already charged a former White House teleprompter operator and ex-Rep. George Santos over trades tied to advance knowledge of Kalshi 'mention markets'.
Agency is telling exchanges to check whether whoever controls a contract's outcome has independent obligations (e.g., a job or fiduciary duty) that would deter manipulation.

items.title: Circle's Bitcoin-Backed USDC Borrowing Gains Traction
points: Circle launched Bitcoin-backed USDC borrowing for Mint clients via Morpho's Arc market, wrapping deposited BTC as 'cirBTC' collateral.
The cirBTC/USDC market grew ~10x in five days: from $1.37M (Sept 17) to $14.3M borrowed USDC against 287 cirBTC tokens.
Galaxy and Keyrock supply dollar liquidity, Circle handles cirBTC issuance and wallets, and Morpho sets loan terms.
Lets institutional Bitcoin holders access USDC (a US-dollar-pegged stablecoin) without selling their BTC.

items.title: CME Expands Crypto Derivatives with Altcoin Futures
points: CME plans to list Bitcoin Cash and Uniswap futures on October 19, pending regulatory approval.
Standard/Micro contract sizes: 250/25 BCH and 10,000/1,000 UNI.
This brings CME's single-asset crypto derivatives roster to 11 tokens; Uniswap is the first DEX (decentralized exchange) governance token CME has listed.
CME's altcoin contracts generated over $1B in notional value this year, averaging 279,800 contracts/day in H1 2026 (~$8.3B daily notional).

items.title: BitMEX Shuts Down Exchange Operations
points: BitMEX ceased exchange operations as of September 23, marking another contraction in the crypto derivatives trading landscape.
